subject: art-design
title: Sketchbook Practice and the Working Wall
welcome_lead: The sketchbook is the laboratory of the artist's mind.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: sketchbook practice, research, and the working wall.

concepts.def: Personal visual journal recording research, ideas, and experimentation.
First-hand observation — photographs, drawings made by the candidate.
Existing images and texts — books, web, gallery research.
Written reflection linking image, intention, and artist research.
Pinned arrangement showing progress, links and curatorial thinking.
Repeated revision and refinement of an idea across studies.

walkthroughs.body_html: A-Level Art assessment objectives reward development, experimentation, recording and realisation. The sketchbook evidences all four — annotated, dated, ordered.
Strong work prioritises primary sources: drawings from life, photographs taken by the candidate, recorded objects. Secondary sources contextualise but should not dominate.
Pinning work to a working wall externalises decisions — scale, sequence, colour relationships and curatorial judgement become visible. It mimics professional studio practice.
